say: Shoot in daylight near a window, not in harsh midday sun or yellow bulb light. Use a plain background so the outfit stands out.

say: Clients ask the same questions: how much, how long, can you make it in my size? Answer them in the entry.
Kemi shows the front and back, plus close-ups of the lined, overlocked inside.
Her prices come from her costing sheet: from 25,000 naira with the client's fabric, and from 48,000 for the full package.
She adds: ready in 10 days after deposit and fitting, with one free adjustment within 7 days. Her chats now move faster from question to deposit.
Clients rarely pay for stitches. They pay for how they look at the event, and for confidence it will be ready. When you only talk price, they compare only cost.
So talk about fit, finish, reliability and aftercare. When she says please reduce it, never go below your total cost.
Say, I can do it at 35,000 without the lining. Or keep the price and add value, like a matching headwrap.
Group orders need a written proposal. Blessing starts from her real costing sheet.

say: Watch for payment scams. Confirm every payment in your app, never from an alert or screenshot.
If someone overpays and asks for a refund, wait until the money clears, and refund only to the same account. No real bank will ask for your PIN, password or OTP.

panel.heading: Taking payments safely

Never share PIN, password or OTP
Receipt sent, cash book updated

say: For example, Ada in Onitsha plans one focus per month, each with a number to check. First, she fixes pricing, because growth on weak pricing only multiplies losses.

cards.d: Fix pricing on two underpriced styles. Target: average order up from 20,000 to 23,000 naira.
Post two garments a week and ask every client for a review. Target: 6 new enquiries a week.
Train her apprentice to finish hems and press. Target: on-time rate above 90%.

say: Next, she builds sales with regular posts, new catalogue items and reviews.
